Abnormalities in the rhythm of the heart include conditions such as unspecified tachycardia, unspecified bradycardia, palpitations, and other or unspecified irregularities in heartbeat patterns. 2. Cardiac murmurs and other heart sounds can be classified as benign or innocent murmurs, unspecified murmurs (including nonspecific cardiac bruits), and other abnormal cardiac sounds. 3. Gangrene, when not classified elsewhere, refers to tissue death due to loss of blood supply. 4. 5. Hemorrhages from the respiratory passages include epistaxis (nosebleeds), throat hemorrhages, hemoptysis (coughing up blood), bleeding from other respiratory sites, and unspecified respiratory hemorrhages. 6. Cough is a symptom that may arise from various underlying conditions. 7. Breathing abnormalities encompass dyspnea (shortness of breath), orthopnea (difficulty breathing when lying flat), stridor (a high-pitched wheezing sound), wheezing, periodic breathing patterns such as Cheyne-Stokes respiration, hyperventilation, mouth breathing, snoring, hiccups, sneezing, and other unspecified breathing irregularities, including sensations of choking. 8. Pain in the throat and chest includes throat pain, chest pain during breathing, precordial pain (localized chest pain), other types of chest pain, and unspecified chest pain. 9. Other symptoms involving the circulatory and respiratory systems include asphyxia, pleurisy (inflammation of the pleura), respiratory arrest, abnormal sputum production, and other specified signs such as rales (crackling lung sounds) and arterial bruits. 10. Abdominal and pelvic pain can manifest as acute abdomen, pain localized to the upper abdomen, pelvic or perineal pain, pain in other parts of the lower abdomen, or other unspecified abdominal pain. 11. Nausea and vomiting are common symptoms of various conditions. 12. Heartburn refers to a burning sensation in the chest due to acid reflux. 13. Dysphagia is difficulty swallowing. 14. Flatulence and related conditions include eructation (belching). 15. Fecal incontinence, also known as encopresis, is the inability to control bowel movements. 16. Hepatomegaly (enlarged liver), splenomegaly (enlarged spleen), or hepatosplenomegaly (enlargement of both liver and spleen) may occur without a specific classification. 17. Unspecified jaundice refers to yellowing of the skin and eyes without a clear cause. 18. Ascites is the accumulation of fluid in the abdominal cavity. 19. Other digestive and abdominal symptoms include intra-abdominal or pelvic swelling, abnormal bowel sounds, visible peristalsis, abdominal rigidity, changes in bowel habits, abnormal fecal characteristics, halitosis (bad breath), and other specified symptoms. 20. Disturbances in skin sensation include anesthesia (loss of sensation), hypoesthesia (reduced sensation), paresthesia (tingling or prickling), hyperesthesia (increased sensitivity), and other unspecified sensory abnormalities. 21. Skin changes include rashes, localized swelling or lumps, cyanosis (bluish discoloration), pallor (paleness), flushing, spontaneous ecchymoses (bruising), petechiae (small red or purple spots), changes in skin texture such as desquamation (peeling) or induration (hardening), and other unspecified changes. 22. Abnormal involuntary movements include abnormal head movements, unspecified tremors, cramps and spasms, fasciculations (muscle twitches), and other unspecified involuntary movements. 23. Gait and mobility abnormalities include ataxic gait (uncoordinated walking), paralytic gait, difficulty walking not classified elsewhere, and other unspecified mobility issues. 24. Lack of coordination includes unspecified ataxia and other unspecified coordination deficits. 25. Other nervous and musculoskeletal symptoms include tetany (muscle spasms), meningismus (meningeal irritation), abnormal reflexes such as hyperreflexia, abnormal posture, clicking hip, and other unspecified signs. 26. Pain during urination includes dysuria, vesical tenesmus (bladder discomfort), and unspecified painful urination. 27. Unspecified hematuria refers to blood in the urine without a clear cause. 28. Unspecified urinary incontinence is the involuntary leakage of urine. 29. Retention of urine refers to the inability to empty the bladder. 30. Anuria and oliguria describe the absence or reduced production of urine, respectively. 31. Polyuria (excessive urination) and nocturia (frequent nighttime urination) are common urinary symptoms. 32. Urethral discharge may indicate infection or other conditions. 33. Other urinary symptoms include extravasation of urine (leakage outside the urinary tract), difficulties with urination, extrarenal uremia (accumulation of waste products), and other unspecified signs. 34. Somnolence, stupor, and coma represent varying levels of impaired consciousness. 35. Cognitive and awareness symptoms include disorientation, anterograde or retrograde amnesia, other memory impairments, and other unspecified cognitive issues. 36. Dizziness and giddiness, including vertigo, are common vestibular symptoms. 37. Disturbances in smell and taste include anosmia (loss of smell), parosmia (distorted smell), parageusia (distorted taste), and other unspecified abnormalities. 38. Hallucinations may be auditory, visual, or of other types, and can also be unspecified. 39. Emotional symptoms include nervousness, restlessness, unhappiness, demoralization, irritability, hostility, physical violence, emotional shock, and other unspecified emotional states. 40. Behavioral symptoms include poor hygiene, bizarre appearance, strange behavior, overactivity, slowness, suspiciousness, undue concern, verbosity, and other unspecified behaviors. 41. Speech disturbances include dysphasia, aphasia, dysarthria, anarthria, and other unspecified speech issues. 42. Symbolic dysfunctions include dyslexia, alexia, agnosia, apraxia, acalculia, and agraphia. 43. Voice disturbances include dysphonia, aphonia, hypernasality, hyponasality, and other unspecified voice issues. 44. Fever of unknown origin may present with chills, persist, or remain unspecified. 45. Pain not classified elsewhere includes acute, chronic intractable, other chronic, and unspecified pain. 46. Malaise and fatigue are nonspecific symptoms of various conditions. 47. Senility refers to age-related cognitive decline. 48. Syncope and collapse describe fainting or sudden loss of consciousness. 49. Convulsions include febrile seizures and other unspecified types. 50. Shock includes cardiogenic, hypovolemic, other types, and unspecified shock. 51. Hemorrhage not classified elsewhere refers to bleeding without a specific cause. 52. Enlarged lymph nodes may be localized, generalized, or unspecified. 53. Edema includes localized, generalized, or unspecified swelling. 54. Hyperhidrosis (excessive sweating) may be localized, generalized, or unspecified, and can include night sweats. 55. Delayed physiological development includes delayed milestones, lack of growth, or unspecified developmental delays. 56. Food and fluid intake symptoms include anorexia, polydipsia (excessive thirst), polyphagia (excessive hunger), feeding difficulties, abnormal weight loss or gain, and other unspecified issues. 57. Cachexia refers to severe weight loss and muscle wasting. 58. General symptoms include hypothermia, nonspecific infant symptoms, dry mouth, clubbing of fingers, and other unspecified signs. 59. Abnormal blood findings include elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, abnormal plasma viscosity, anisocytosis, poikilocytosis, and other abnormalities in red or white blood cells. 60. Elevated blood glucose levels include abnormal glucose tolerance, prediabetes, and unspecified hyperglycemia. 61. Abnormal serum enzyme levels include elevated transaminases, LDH, acid phosphatase, alkaline phosphatase, amylase, and lipase. 62. Abnormal immunological findings include raised antibody titers, abnormal tuberculin reactions, false-positive syphilis tests, and other unspecified findings. 63. Abnormal plasma proteins include albumin, globulin, alpha-fetoprotein, and other unspecified abnormalities. 64. Findings of substances in blood include alcohol, opiates, cocaine, hallucinogens, psychotropic drugs, steroids, heavy metals, and other unspecified substances. 65. Abnormal blood chemistry includes abnormal mineral levels, blood gas levels, and other unspecified findings. 66. Abnormal urine findings include proteinuria, glycosuria, chyluria, myoglobinuria, biliuria, hemoglobinuria, ketonuria, elevated drug levels, and other unspecified abnormalities. 67. Abnormal findings in cerebrospinal fluid, respiratory specimens, digestive specimens, and genital specimens may indicate underlying pathology. 68. Abnormal diagnostic imaging findings include intracranial lesions, lung abnormalities, breast abnormalities, and other structural issues. 69. Abnormal function studies include abnormal EEG, pulmonary function, cardiovascular function, renal function, liver function, thyroid function, and other endocrine studies. 70. Ill-defined causes of mortality include sudden infant death syndrome, instantaneous death, unattended death, and other unspecified causes.
